unit.coverage_note: The 8 tests map 1:1 onto the ticket's three stated failure modes, plus the two subtle state rules the implementation comments call out (a superseded request completing must NOT clear `pending`; complete() is idempotent). That is unusually tight test-to-requirement traceability.

notes.title: AbortSignal support is not implemented, and the stated reason is correct
notes.detail: The ticket offered an alternative shape 'with AbortSignal support so the in-flight request can actually be cancelled rather than just discarded'. The implementation declines it, documenting: 'the generated API clients build their own RequestInit and take no AbortSignal, so there is nothing to cancel through.' I VERIFIED that claim rather than accepting it: in core/api/platform.ts the generated methods take only domain parameters (e.g. signIn(authenticationType?, returnUrl?, storeId?, ...)) with no per-call options argument, each builds `let options_: RequestInit = { method, headers }` locally, and the file's single 'signal' occurrence (line 794) is an unrelated doc comment. The two extension points that do exist - the protected transformOptions(options) hook and the injectable http.fetch in the constructor - are both PER-CLIENT, not per-call, so neither could cancel an individual request. The rationale holds fully. Discarding rather than aborting is the correct call for this client generation.

notes.severity: informational - deviation from the proposal, an improvement
notes.title: pending is exposed as a readonly Ref, not the proposed callback
notes.detail: The ticket sketched `useLatestRequest((pending) => { loading.value = pending; })` - a callback parameter. The implementation instead exposes `pending: Readonly<Ref<boolean>>`. This is more Vue-idiomatic (composes with watch/computed, no wiring boilerplate) and the ticket said 'roughly', so it is a sound deviation rather than a miss. Worth recording only so nobody reads the ticket later and thinks the callback form is missing.

notes.title: The primitive has ZERO consumers in the framework itself
notes.detail: grep across the whole vc-shell repo finds `useLatestRequest` only in the barrel export line and two CHANGELOG entries - no framework component or composable uses it. So its behaviour is exercised only by its own unit tests; there is no integration evidence in-tree. This is NOT an AC failure - the ticket asked for a primitive so MODULES stop reimplementing it, not for internal adoption. Recording it because the framework does contain blades of exactly the shape the ticket describes (search + pagination + details), so a follow-up audit for latent races in-framework may be worthwhile. I did not attempt to find such a race and am not claiming one exists.

notes.title: The one motivating consumer (PR #159) is still OPEN and has not migrated - a window to PREVENT the duplication
notes.detail: The ticket's evidence base is vc-module-pagebuilder's own src/utilities/latestRequest.ts ('4 call sites across two modules', 'fixed a real pre-existing stale-response race in its asset library'). That file does NOT exist on vc-module-pagebuilder@dev: the shell app's src/ has no utilities/ directory, and two code searches returned zero. The reason is that PR #159 (feat(VCST-4933): add Page Builder Shared Components) is still OPEN - created 2026-07-31, merged_at null, last updated 2026-08-13 10:08. The framework primitive landed 2026-08-13 17:22, about seven hours AFTER #159 was last touched, and #159 has not moved since. So the duplication this TechDebt describes has never actually shipped - it is still prospective, sitting on an unmerged branch. That is the useful part: rather than paying the debt down later, #159 can be migrated to the framework's useLatestRequest BEFORE it merges, and the duplicate helper never enters the codebase. The reviewer already assigned to #159 is the same developer who wrote the primitive.
